transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I feel like the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and come back. I’m pretty sure they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps saying it’s just regular notices on the doors, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?
I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal sounds around the building, but I can’t say I’ve heard voices that nobody else could hear.
Do you think these people are watching you for a specific reason?

I think it’s because they’re keeping track of me. Like when I leave and when I come back, they notice it, and then I believe they’re passing notes about me to the office. They say it’s just regular notices on the doors, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Have you ever thought that maybe you're mistaken about people watching you and passing notes?

I’ve thought about it because people keep telling me that, but I don’t really believe I’m mistaken. It feels clear to me that they’re watching when I leave and come back, and those notes on the doors are about me getting passed to the office.
Do you think there's a larger plan or scheme involved in the people watching you and passing notes?

I don’t know if I’d call it a whole big scheme, but it feels organized enough. The people at my apartment are watching when I leave and come back, and I believe they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps saying they’re just notices on the doors, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.
Do you think these beliefs about being watched and the notes being passed are connected to something specific about you, like who you are or something you've done?

I’m not sure it’s about something I did exactly. It’s more like they’re focused on me, on when I leave and when I come back. I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching that and slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody says it’s just notices on the doors, but I don’t believe that.
Do you think it would make sense to other people that the apartment staff would be watching you and passing notes about you to the office?

Maybe not to everybody, no. They keep telling me it’s just notices on the doors, so I know they don’t see it the way I do. But to me it makes sense, because I know they’re watching when I leave and come back and passing notes about me to the office.
Do you think your beliefs about being watched and the notes could change if you found out more information?

I don’t know. I mean, people keep telling me they’re just notices on the doors, but I still feel like they’re watching when I come and go and passing notes about me to the office. If I saw something that really proved otherwise, maybe, but right now I believe what I’m seeing.
If someone showed you proof that the notes on the doors were actually just regular notices and not about you, would you still believe that people are watching you?

Yeah… I think I still would. Maybe the papers on the doors could be regular notices, but that doesn’t change that I feel like they’re watching when I leave and when I come back. That part is what I’m sure about.
Would anything be able to convince you that the people at your apartment are not watching you?

I don’t know what would convince me, honestly. Everybody keeps saying it’s just notices on the doors, but I came in because I know they’re watching when I leave and come back, and I believe they’re slipping notes about me to the office. So… no, not really, not right now.
If someone you trusted completely told you that they had proof that nobody was watching you, would you believe them?

I’d want to trust them, but… I don’t think I’d believe it all the way. I came in because I know people at my apartment are watching when I leave and come back, and I think they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Even if somebody said they had proof, it would be hard for me to accept that.
Do you think the idea of your apartment neighbors watching you and passing notes to the office is something that could happen in real life?

Yes, I do. I mean, people can watch who’s coming and going, and they can pass things to the office. That’s why I came in — because I know they’re watching me when I leave and come back, and I believe those notes are about me, even though everybody keeps saying they’re just regular notices on the doors.
How certain are you that people are watching you and passing notes about you to the office?

I’m pretty certain. I mean, to me it’s not just a maybe. I came in because I know they’re watching when I leave and come back, and I believe they’re slipping notes about me to the office. People keep telling me it’s just notices on the doors, but I don’t see it that way.
Would you say the idea that your neighbors are watching you and passing notes about you to the office is a strange or unusual belief to have?

I guess other people might think it sounds unusual, yeah. But to me it doesn’t feel strange, because I know what I’ve been seeing — them watching when I leave and come back, and those notes going to the office. Everybody says they’re just regular notices on the doors, but I don’t believe that.

Would you describe the idea that your neighbors are watching you and passing notes about you to the office as something that could happen to anyone, or is it a belief that is very unique to your situation?

I think it could happen to anyone in a building, people watching who comes and goes. But this feels like it’s about me, my situation. I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching me and slipping notes about me to the office, even though everyone keeps saying they’re just regular notices on the doors.
Do you think your belief about being watched would change even if everything in your life returned to normal and nothing out of the ordinary happened for a long time?

I don’t think it would change much, no. Even if things got quiet for a while, I’d still know what I saw at my apartment — people watching when I come and go, and those notes going to the office. Everybody keeps saying they’re just notices on the doors, but that’s not how it looks to me.
Would you describe the people watching you and passing notes about you as being part of a normal, everyday activity that most people would understand?

No, I wouldn’t call it normal everyday stuff. I mean, they say it’s just notices on the doors, but that’s not what I see. I came in because I know they’re watching when I leave and come back, and slipping notes about me to the office.
Do you think there's anything that could ever make you completely stop believing that people are watching you and passing notes about you?

I don’t really think so. I mean, people can keep telling me they’re just notices on the doors, but I know what I’ve seen. They watch when I come and go, and those notes go to the office about me. I don’t know what would make me stop believing that.
Is there anything that could potentially happen in the future that would make you realize that your beliefs about being watched are not true?

I don’t know what could happen that would make me think it wasn’t true. I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching when I leave and come back, and I’ve seen the notes going to the office. Everybody keeps saying they’re just notices on the doors, but that’s not how it seems to me.
Do you think your beliefs about being watched would be considered reasonable by most people?

Most people probably wouldn’t see it the way I do, no. They keep saying it’s just notices on the doors, but I know what’s happening at my apartment. They’re watching when I come and go, and those notes are about me going to the office.
